record.paper_title: The Flow Associated to Weakly Differentiable Vector Fields: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let ν be a regular measure on P(R^d), meaning that its expectation Eν is bounded above by C·L^d for some constant C. Can there exist a ν-regular Lagrangian flow μ in P(R^d) that is not induced by any L^d-regular Lagrangian flow X in R^d via the formula μ(t,μ)=∫_{R^d} δ_{X(t,x)} dμ(x)?

evidence.quote: We say that ν ∈ M+(P(Rd)) is regular if Eν ≤ CLd for some constant C.
one may speculate about situations where a ν-RLF µ exists in P(Rd), with ν regular, but the flow µ is not induced by any Ld-RLF X as in (5.3).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \ge 1$ and let $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ denote the space of Borel probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$, equipped with its natural Polish topology. Let $\mathcal{M}_+(\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d))$ denote the set of nonnegative finite Borel measures on $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$. For $\nu \in \mathcal{M}_+(\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d))$, define its expectation $\mathbb{E}\nu \in \mathcal{M}_+(\mathbb{R}^d)$ by
$$\mathbb{E}\nu(A) := \int_{\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)} \mu(A)\, d\nu(\mu), \qquad A \subset \mathbb{R}^d \text{ Borel}.$$
Call $\nu$ regular if $\mathbb{E}\nu \le C \mathcal{L}^d$ for some constant $C \ge 0$, where $\mathcal{L}^d$ denotes Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$.

Fix a Borel time-dependent vector field $b:[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$. An $\mathcal{L}^d$-regular Lagrangian flow (RLF) for $b$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is a Borel map $X:[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ such that:
(i) for $\mathcal{L}^d$-a.e. $x$, $t\mapsto X(t,x)$ is an absolutely continuous integral solution of $\dot\gamma(t)=b(t,\gamma(t))$ with $\gamma(0)=x$; and
(ii) there is $L\ge 0$ with $X(t,\cdot)_\#\mathcal{L}^d \le L\,\mathcal{L}^d$ for every $t\in[0,T]$.

Lift $b$ to a vector field $B$ on $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ (in the sense used in continuity-equation theory on Wasserstein space). A $\nu$-regular Lagrangian flow for $B$ in $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ is a Borel map $\boldsymbol{\mu}:[0,T]\times\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)\to\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ such that:
(i') for $\nu$-a.e. $\mu$, $t\mapsto\boldsymbol{\mu}(t,\mu)$ is an integral curve of $B$ starting at $\mu$; and
(ii') $\boldsymbol{\mu}(t,\cdot)_\#\nu$ is regular with a uniform bound in $t$.

Given an $\mathcal{L}^d$-RLF $X$, one induces a flow on $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ by
$$\boldsymbol{\mu}(t,\mu) := \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\delta_{X(t,x)}\,d\mu(x). \qquad (*)$$

Question: Does there exist a regular $\nu$ and a $\nu$-regular Lagrangian flow $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ in $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ that is not of the form $(*)$ for any $\mathcal{L}^d$-regular Lagrangian flow $X$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns existence of genuinely "higher-level" regular Lagrangian flows on the space of probability measures that are not lifts of classical RLFs on $\mathbb{R}^d$. It is posed as a speculative open problem in surveys on flows of weakly differentiable vector fields, and no resolution appears in the literature available via search.

status_evidence.title: The flow associated to weakly differentiable vector fields: recent results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems about regular Lagrangian flows, including higher-level flows on P(R^d).
status_evidence.claim: The question is presented as an open speculative problem about ν-RLFs not induced by L^d-RLFs.
